data.name: Sakshi
data.gender_notes: Sakshi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who sees, observes, or witnesses. Can refer to a deity, a divine witness, or an observer in a spiritual or metaphysical context. The name Sakshi carries the meaning “Witness, Observer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sakshi usually hope their child will grow to embody witness, observer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Refers to the divine witness consciousness that observes the universe and all beings.
data.etymology: Sakshi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Witness, Observer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sakshi total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sakshi holds significant importance in Hindu culture, representing one's role as a witness in various aspects of life, including religious ceremonies, court proceedings, and personal experiences. The concept of a divine witness is also a common theme in Hindu mythology and philosophy, where gods and goddesses serve as witnesses to the actions and deeds of devotees and other beings.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Sakshi carries a profound meaning as it relates to the concept of self-awareness and the innate ability of the soul to witness and observe the actions of both the self and the external world. It signifies the ultimate reality of consciousness and underlines the impermanence of material existence, leading to a greater understanding of the self and the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sakshi represents the divine Witness, the eternal Observer within us, beyond the transient self. It symbolizes the pure consciousness that transcends the physical world and remains untouched by the cycle of birth and death.
